The verdict is the same either way

How to fix it

Round the sharp inside corner to a 2.71 mm radius
Stress piles up in the sharp inside corner. A fillet of 2.71 mm (about half the 5.41 mm wall) spreads it out.
Thicken the wall at the peak from 5.41 to 8.02 mm
The wall through the peak is 5.41 mm. To reach safety factor 2.5 it needs 8.02 mm (+48%), because bending stress falls with thickness squared.
Add a triangular gusset across the inside corner
The peak sits where two walls meet and bend. A gusset as thick as the wall, with legs about half as long as the shorter wall, ties them together and usually cuts the corner stress by half or more.

Setup

materialPETG (3D printed)
limit47 MPa
target safety factor2.5
mass34.95 g
load250 N down at 0,-15,31 @ normal +y and box -21,4,10,21,6,52 rigid
fixturebolt holes d=5.5
part9 holes, 1 inside fillets, 2 sharp inside corners, walls about 5 mm

Assumptions

  1. Linear elastic material and small deflections (no yielding redistribution, no buckling).
  2. PETG (3D printed): E 2100 MPa, Poisson 0.38, von Mises vs yield 47 MPa (Prusament PETG technical data sheet).
  3. Loads are static and applied all at once; no impact, vibration or fatigue.
  4. Printed layers stack along z; pull across layers is judged against 70% of the in-plane strength.
  5. Bolted holes are rigidly held over the hole and a washer sized ring (twice the hole radius).
  6. Remote loads reach the part through a rigid attachment (the attached part does not flex).
  7. Contact between separate parts, friction and preload are not modeled.

Notes

  • Built from mount.py with thickness=5, rib=0, fillet=3, height=55.
  • 2 curved elements folded on thin walls, so this mesh uses straight sided second order elements.
Made with Wobbl 0.1.0. Solver CalculiX 2.23. Total time 223 s.
